cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. For tonight's courtyard film, you fold the moon; I'll switch off the lamps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Start with the crescent. It already has a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you'll own the moon. Can I tell the audience we're waiting for your blackout?

mechanism: A assigns the impossible sky task to B and negotiates extra ordinary work only to preserve that assignment.
confusable: Unlike simply asking for help, A insists the one impossible responsibility remain B's when B proposes swapping.
comparison: Audience blackout pressure and moon folding differ from a time-storage task with A doing labels.
seedUse: The seed already divides work, rejects the practical swap and seeks public attribution to B, giving S01 control of responsibility.
